question: Do three non-gated syscall families (mlockall, faccessat2, pidfd_send_signal) with no existing corpus guest hold byte-identical parity under e9patch preprocessing with the golden hermit ptrace backend, after dropping openat2 and System V IPC which hermit does not support?
backend: ptrace (golden reference); e9patch = binary-rewriting preprocessing, not a backend
determinism_level: L2 (--strict --verify, guest-visible bitwise-identical; detlog tail-match modulo 8-syscall e9loader prologue)
dropped: openat2_devnull: openat2(437) returns failure under hermit (unsupported)
shmget_rmid: shmget(29) fails under hermit (no usable System V IPC namespace)
semget_rmid: semget(64) fails under hermit (no usable System V IPC namespace)
msgget_rmid: msgget(68) fails under hermit (no usable System V IPC namespace)
host_independence: prints only syscall return on success (0) or a boolean; fd/id numbers read but not printed
gating: non-gated: memory locking / access check / pidfd signalling touch neither time, randomness, nor CPU scheduling; routine backend-parity, no post-facto-human-review trigger
ci_note: e9tool/e9patch absent from CI (like KVM /dev/kvm); corpus harness ungated, only audit-inventory gates these files
